Subject: Re: Thanks — quick recap + next steps — model shortlist attached

Hi Sarah / David —

Attached is a short PDF (redwood-acme-model-shortlist.pdf) and the raw benchmark CSV. High level recommendations (3 candidates):

1) RW-7B-int8 (cost-first / low-latency)
- Rationale: Best cost per token, lowest end-to-end median latency. Good for short summarization where aggressive prompt engineering + post-filtering reduces hallucinations.
- Ballpark cost: ~$0.60 per 1k tokens (hosted, int8 variant)
- Median latency (256 tokens): ~220ms; (900 tokens): ~700ms
- Quality notes: Slightly more prone to factual drift on long context; recommend prompt templates with explicit grounding and the extracted-entities prefill step.

2) RW-13B-std (balanced)
- Rationale: Good middle ground — improved factuality over 7B while still relatively affordable. Handles longer contexts more gracefully.
- Ballpark cost: ~$1.80 per 1k tokens
- Median latency (256 tokens): ~480ms; (900 tokens): ~1.4s
- Quality notes: Stronger out-of-the-box summaries; fewer hallucinations on multi-turn threads.

3) RW-70B-q4 (quality-first / high-cost)
- Rationale: Best for high-fidelity outputs and edge-case coverage. Useful for compliance-sensitive summaries where recall/precision matter.
- Ballpark cost: ~$6.50 per 1k tokens (quantized runtime)
- Median latency (256 tokens): ~1.8s; (900 tokens): ~5.5s
- Quality notes: Lowest hallucination rate in our benchmark set; recommended for canary on high-value flows.

Notes on quantization & regression risks:
- Quantized runtimes (int8 / q4) significantly reduce cost and memory but can alter token logits subtly. For most templated summarization prompts we saw <1% drop in automated ROUGE/QA metrics versus fp16; for adversarial / low-resource prompts there can be higher variance.
- We recommend a short regression suite (we included a recommended prompt set in acme-prompt-sets.zip) to run against any candidate to detect quality regressions before rollout.

Attachments included: redwood-acme-model-shortlist.pdf (shortlist + charts), acme-benchmarks-20260304.csv (raw evals), acme-prompt-sets.zip (prompt templates + failure cases).

Links / reproducible artifacts:
- Evaluation folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-eval-pack-acme
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/ACME-2026-001

Proposed next step: we can run a 48-72 hour evaluation on your data (we’ll run the three candidates on the shared prompt set, produce token-level cost, latency distribution, and a small human review of 50 sample outputs). If you’re +1 I’ll open the eval job and assign an early results checkpoint.

If helpful I can also set up a short runbook for canary config (batching, cache TTLs, and fallback policy).

Best,
Marissa
